git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0.git "$HOME/cube"
cd "$HOME/cube"

git checkout 446ebe396489ca75679caa80887d7257efe92e3d
git submodule update --init --depth 1 Drivers/BSP/STM32G0xx_Nucleo
WS=$HOME/ccs-workspace
mkdir -p "$WS/.claude/skills"
cp -R "/Applications/ti/ccs2101/ccs/Code Composer Studio.app/Contents/Resources/ai/skills.alpha/ti-ccstudio-migrate-to-ti" "$WS/.claude/skills/"

rows.name: Arduino sketches on the LP-EM-CC2340R5 and LP-MSPM0G3519 through the Zephyr-based core: Blink and AnalogReadSerial
rows.headline: Arduino's stock Blink and AnalogReadSerial run unchanged on the LP-EM-CC2340R5 and LP-MSPM0G3519 through the Zephyr-based core.
rows.changed: A pin-map overlay per board, an app CMake file that includes the .ino as it is, and an optional six-line patch so Serial blocks instead of dropping bytes. The G3519 also needed its ADC12 node switched on in the overlay (driver in Zephyr main only).
rows.effort: About two hours for both boards, including the G3519 ADC overlay and a Serial fix
rows.from: ArduinoCore-zephyr af5b8610f9be (Apache-2.0), ArduinoCore-API 1.5.2, arduino-examples (public domain sketches)
rows.broke: Serial drops bytes at 9600 baud with the shipped core (patch fixes it). Zephyr 4.4.2 has no MSPM0 ADC or I2C, so the G3519 needs Zephyr main plus the open MSPM0 I2C pull request. The G3519 image stops in the NMI handler unless nRST is pulsed after the DSLite flash. Found upstream: the CC23 GPIO driver clears edge detect on any pin reconfigure; the CC2340R5 board file maps the red PWM LED to a timer channel that does not reach the pin; the shared MSPM0 pin file gives PB27 a function that is not the timer on the G351x; the MSPM0 GPIO driver keeps old edge bits; the MSPM0 PWM driver inverts duty; the core's transfer(buf, n) splits the write and the read. CC2340R5 SPI data not checked (no loopback wire); no I2C device was on its bus; LEDs not seen.

build.note: Blink and AnalogReadSerial, Zephyr 4.4.2, GCC 12.2

memory.note: 27.7 to 37.4 kB flash, 5.2 to 6.1 kB RAM

function.note: Blink toggled DIO15; AnalogReadSerial printed values at 9600 baud

uart.note: Serial at 9600 baud on the backchannel; 6 line ends in 2.5 kB until the blocking-write patch

i2c_spi.note: Wire scan of an empty bus returns 0 devices; sensor read waits on the bench; SPI.transfer of 8 bytes completes; data unchecked without a loopback wire

timers_pwm.note: analogWrite on both LEDs; timer period and compare registers read back as set; LED not seen

interrupts.note: attachInterrupt on S1 (DIO10), 10 of 10 software-triggered edges

build.note: Blink and AnalogReadSerial, Zephyr main 4.5.0-dev

memory.note: 22.8 to 31.1 kB flash, 4.8 kB RAM

function.note: PB27 toggled; AnalogReadSerial printed values

uart.note: Serial at 9600 baud on the backchannel

i2c_spi.note: Wire reads the FT6336U at 0x38 on PC2/PC3 (vendor 0x11, chip 0x64), 100 of 100, 489 us a read; SPI0 loopback bit: 256 of 256 bytes and transfer16 equal; transfer(buf, n) returns zeros

timers_pwm.note: analogWrite on PB27 with pin function 9; duty measured inverted by the driver; LED not seen

interrupts.note: attachInterrupt on S2 (PB3), 10 of 10 software-triggered edges; a second mode keeps the old edges

rows.command:
export AM=$HOME/zr-arduino ZP=$HOME/zephyrproject TC=$HOME/zephyr-toolchain
git init "$AM" && git -C "$AM" remote add origin https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/ArduinoCore-zephyr.git
git -C "$AM" fetch --depth 1 origin af5b8610f9be6d7b962e2ba6dd8e6859697c44ff && git -C "$AM" checkout FETCH_HEAD
mkdir -p "$AM/zephyr/blobs" && cp -R third-party/arduino/ArduinoCore-API/api "$AM/zephyr/blobs/ArduinoCore-API"
git -C "$AM" apply "$PWD/portability/arduino/zephyr/serial-blocking-write.patch"
portability/arduino/zephyr/build-cc2340r5.sh Blink
rows.see: Blink toggles the board's LED pin; AnalogReadSerial prints 10-bit readings at 9600 baud on the probe's serial port.
rows.numbers: Images are 22.8 to 38.3 kB of flash and 4.8 to 6.1 kB of RAM. On the LP-MSPM0G3519, Wire reads the touch controller 100 of 100 times and SPI loopback returns 256 of 256 bytes.

rows.name: Renesas FSP examples (UART, ADC, I2C, GPT timer) on the LP-MSPM0G3519
rows.headline: Four of five Renesas FSP examples (FSP is Renesas's driver layer) run on the LP-MSPM0G3519 on a layer that maps FSP calls onto DriverLib, TI's register-level driver library.
rows.changed: A 577-line FSP-on-DriverLib layer (about 70 lines map the RA event link and transfer controller onto MSPM0 events and DMA) plus a 189-line board file; five constants in iic_master for the FT6336U instead of the ADXL345.
rows.effort: About four hours for the five examples
rows.from: renesas/ra-fsp-examples c74f31fde (BSD-3-Clause)
rows.broke: The unchanged iic_master reports a missing ADXL345 and then prints 65535 for every axis, because the upstream example treats a bad ID read as success. The FT6336U needs about 400 ms after its reset line goes high. adc_gpt_periodic_sampling: two DMA channels on one ADC trigger fill group A at half rate and group B never completes (cause not found). The timer runs 0.55 percent short against the Mac clock (internal oscillator). The ADC input was floating. LED not seen.

build.note: sci_uart, adc, iic_master with TI Arm Clang through the layer

memory.note: 12.4 to 15.5 kB flash, 511 B to 4.7 kB RAM

function.note: sci_uart accepts 1 to 100 and refuses 0, abc, 101, 12.5 as upstream; PB27 duty measured 0.9 to 99.9 percent

adc.note: single scan on a floating A0 (PA27), counts 306 and 493; continuous and window compare not run

i2c_spi.note: iic_master reads FT6336U ID 0x64 at 0x38, 3 runs identical

uart.note: console on the XDS110 backchannel

timers_pwm.note: gpt periodic, PWM and one-shot modes; PWM 0.89 to 100.00 percent high at 1 kHz on PB27; LED not seen

dma.note: timer to ADC to DMA event link: 1,023 intervals within 2 counts, none missed (one channel); the two-channel group chain does not complete

rows.see: The example reads the touch controller at 0x38 on the Waveshare panel and prints on the serial port at 115200 baud.
rows.numbers: sci_uart, adc and gpt run with no edit, and iic_master with five constants changed for the touch controller. Flash use is 12.4 to 15.5 kB.
rows.limits: The fifth example, timer-triggered ADC, runs up to its DMA chain, and its two-group DMA transfer does not complete. The unchanged iic_master reports a missing ADXL345.

rows.name: Raspberry Pi Pico SDK examples on the LP-MSPM0G3519
rows.headline: Raspberry Pi pico-examples (serial hello, I2C bus scan, blink, PWM fade, ADC read) run unchanged on the LP-MSPM0G3519 over a thin layer on DriverLib.
rows.changed: A 316-line layer of Pico SDK headers and functions over DriverLib (pico/stdlib, hardware/gpio, uart, i2c, pwm, adc, pico/time) plus 81 lines of board files mapping Pico GPIO numbers to G3519 pins; the real pico-sdk supplies only pico/error.h and pico/binary_info.h.
rows.effort: About two hours for the five examples
rows.from: raspberrypi/pico-examples 0d62f75 and pico-sdk 2.3.1 (BSD-3-Clause)
rows.broke: A puts/fputs link clash, the 256-byte default linker stack and a PWM reset bug in the layer, all fixed. No PIO equivalent. LED not watched; ADC input floating; the fade rate is computed.

build.note: five examples, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS, MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07

memory.note: 1.8 to 10.6 kB flash, 2.1 to 2.4 kB RAM including a 2 kB stack

gpio.note: blink_simple: PB27 changed 10 times in 12 samples

uart.note: hello_world/serial, one line a second

timers_pwm.note: pwm/led_fade wrap interrupt updates the compare register

adc.note: adc/hello_adc reads every 0.5 s, floating input

rows.command:
export PICO_SDK=$HOME/pico-sdk OUT=$PWD/out/pico
git clone --depth 1 --branch 2.3.1 https://github.com/raspberrypi/pico-sdk.git "$PICO_SDK"
portability/pico-on-mspm0/build.sh bus_scan
rows.see: bus_scan finds the touch controller at 0x38 and nothing else; hello_serial prints "Hello, world!" once a second on the probe's serial port.
rows.numbers: The layer is 316 lines plus 81 lines of board files. The five examples take 1.8 to 10.6 kB of flash.
rows.limits: There is no PIO equivalent.

rows.name: SimpleFOC motor-control library on the LP-AM13E230 with the DRV8376EVM
rows.headline: SimpleFOC 2.4.0 builds for the LP-AM13E230 with none of its files changed: 23.1 kB of flash, 160 lines of port code, and a 6.7 us (open loop) or 9.6 us (Hall velocity loop) pass on the 200 MHz core. The motor has not turned: the supply was off.
rows.changed: Nothing in SimpleFOC. The chip layer implements its hardware_api.h 6-PWM functions on MCPWM4 and its few Arduino calls on the DWT counter and GPIO; a 62-line Arduino.h holds constants and a Print that discards text.
rows.effort: One working session
rows.from: SimpleFOC Arduino-FOC 2.4.0, commit b3d8f39 (MIT)
rows.broke: No motor run yet (bus 3.7 V, supply off), so no speed ripple or current; voltage mode only, no current sensing layer; Hall angle is SimpleFOC's 60 degree steps.
rows.numbers: 23,084 B of flash against 61.7 kB for TI's Hall FOC image; 6.74 us per loop pass open loop, 9.58 us closed loop on the Halls, motor supply off.
rows.limits: Spin, speed ripple and current are waiting for the motor supply; current-sense mode is not written.

build.note: 5 s build with TI Arm Clang; 0 SimpleFOC lines changed

memory.note: 23,084 B flash

timers_pwm.note: MCPWM4 driven through hardware_api.h; loop passes run at 20 kHz PWM with the supply off

rows.name: Zephyr on the AM62L's Cortex-A53: from on-chip SRAM, and on one core beside Linux
rows.headline: Zephyr's upstream am62l_evm board runs with no DDR, no TF-A and no TIFS: a 124 KB hello world in the 144 KB of on-chip SRAM, started over JTAG at EL3. A second build runs on A53 core 1 from DDR, started by a PSCI call from U-Boot, and keeps ticking while Linux boots and runs on core 0 with no hypervisor.
rows.changed: Two overlays and two config files in am62l-evm/zephyr/ (one core, EL3 entry, no SCMI or PSCI, UART0 only, 8 translation tables; the DDR build adds a console ring and a patch that leaves the GIC distributor to Linux). Zephyr files unmodified.
rows.effort: About a day for the SRAM run; half a day for the core beside Linux
rows.from: Zephyr main a915b2f (its am62l_evm board is written for a start from U-Boot with the DDR up)
rows.broke: The stock CCStudio board file runs the DDR initialization on connect (a copy without the startup script fixes it). The first beside-Linux build in SRAM never ran: Linux and TF-A own that SRAM, so the image moved to DDR. Nothing here measures speed or boot time; the SRAM load went through the debugger, not the boot ROM.

build.note: 124 KB SRAM image, 44.0 kB DDR image; Zephyr a915b2f, GCC 12

function.note: banner and hello line on UART0 from SRAM; tick 0 to 270 in the console ring on core 1 beside Linux

uart.note: UART0 at 115200 with no TIFS or TF-A: an 0x55 stream at 11.6 kB/s, the exact line rate

low_power.note: 552.5 mW with Linux idle on core 0 and the Zephyr hello looping on core 1; 633.5 mW with Zephyr CoreMark on core 1

interrupts.note: Zephyr's own timer tick beside Linux; no other interrupt tried

rtos.note: kernel idle thread reached after main from SRAM; k_busy_wait tick loop beside Linux

rows.see: UART0 prints *** Booting Zephyr OS build a915b2f12675 *** and Hello World! am62l_evm/am62l3/a53 with the DDR never initialized; beside Linux, /dev/mem reads tick lines from core 1's console ring.
rows.numbers: 124 KB image in a 144 KB SRAM map, 20 KB spare. Beside Linux: 44.0 kB in DDR, started by PSCI CPU_ON, 66 console bytes in 3 s while Linux runs; 552.5 mW for the board with both.
rows.limits: One core, UART0 only, no peripheral beyond the timer. The SRAM image was loaded by the debugger, so this shows the chip runs it, not that a product starts that way.

rows.name: TI's Jailhouse hypervisor on the AM62L: bare-metal and Linux cells beside Linux
rows.headline: TI's documented Jailhouse flow from Linux SDK 12.01.00.05.03 ran as written on the AM62L EVM: the hypervisor enabled in 0.27 s, the uart and gic demo cells printed within a second, and a second Linux reached a login about 20 s after its cell started.
rows.changed: Nothing in TI's files. The board booted from a USB stick instead of TI's SD card, with the Jailhouse kernel, device tree, inmate archive and tools copied onto it under new names.
rows.effort: About 15 minutes on the board once the files were on the stick (U-Boot over UART takes 7 minutes)
rows.from: TI's Jailhouse image and Hypervisor page for the AM62L, Linux SDK 12.01.00.05.03
rows.broke: The micro-SD slot would not take the card on hand, so the run boots over UART and a USB stick. No Zephyr cell was built; TI's page names none.

function.note: jailhouse enable, uart-demo, gic-demo, a Linux inmate to login, stop, destroy, disable; every command returned 0

timing.note: enable 0.27 s, disable 0.09 s, Linux inmate to login about 20 s

rtos.note: no Zephyr or FreeRTOS inmate was built; Zephyr has Jailhouse support upstream for other boards

rows.see: UART1 (the FT4232's port B) prints the uart-demo and gic-demo lines, then a second Linux login prompt, while the first Linux stays at its prompt on UART0.
rows.numbers: Hypervisor enable 0.27 s; demo cells print within 1 s; Linux cell to login about 20 s; disable 0.09 s.
rows.limits: No Zephyr cell, no cell-to-cell message traffic, no timing beyond these.

rows.name: Open radar readers on the IWRL6432BOOST: the ROS driver, the Python SDK 3 reader, the gesture recognizer
rows.headline: Once the board sends the standard point format (guiMonitor 1), the most-forked Python mmWave SDK 3 reader reads every point of two recorded walks with its parser unedited; the reference ROS 1 driver publishes every point when frames come every 50 ms, nothing at the board's 250 ms; the most-starred gesture recognizer reads no frame, because it expects an AWR1642 SDK 2 layout and near-field gestures at 10 frames a second.
rows.changed: The Python reader: no source change, NumPy 1.26 and a macOS port wrapper. The ROS driver: C++11 to C++14 in its build file, startup parameters set by hand. The gesture recognizer: not made to run; it needs a format converter and new recordings.
rows.effort: About a day for the three, with the walk recordings re-encoded into the firmware's byte stream
rows.from: ibaiGorordo/AWR1843-Read-Data-Python-MMWAVE-SDK-3- 66f16c2 (Python reader), radar-lab/ti_mmwave_rospkg cb3255f (ROS 1 driver), vilari-mickopf/mmwave-gesture-recognition 07a1ec8
rows.broke: NumPy 2 stops the Python reader at the first point. On macOS the data port reports 0 bytes waiting until a read is issued, so the reader saw nothing live without the wrapper. The ROS driver's serial loop pushes a stale byte on each 100 ms read timeout, so every 250 ms frame fails its length check. The gesture recognizer's config loader stops on a low-power SDK cfg.

function.note: Python reader: 537 frames and 3,489 points from two recordings, identical to the recordings; live, 120 frame headers in 30 s; ROS driver: 265 frames and 1,696 points at 50 ms, identical within 2.4e-7 m, none at 250 ms; gesture recognizer: 0 of 328 frames

uart.note: the board's data port at its shipped rate, read live on macOS through the wrapper

build.note: ROS driver on ROS Noetic in Docker after one build-file edit

rows.see: The Python reader prints frame and point counts that match the recording; the ROS node publishes PointCloud2 on /ti_mmwave/radar_scan_pcl.
rows.numbers: Python reader 537 of 537 frames; ROS driver 265 of 265 frames at 50 ms, 0 at 250 ms; gesture recognizer 0 of 328 frames.
rows.limits: Live points were checked only with nobody in front of the radar. The ROS driver needs frames under 100 ms or a change to its read loop. The gesture recognizer is not running.
